articleBlocks: At first, Vines and Orangutans made this feel like a jungle board. The opening clues stay ambiguous until Old tires gives the board a cleaner test, so this guide starts with the misleading first read, then uses the later clues to show why the final connection is narrower than the early guesses and how each clue checks that same pattern without relying on the answer reveal too early.
That first read held for a moment, especially once Hammocks joined in.
But Old tires changed the solve.
That clue stopped the board from being about a place and pushed it toward an action instead.
An old tire is not just something you find outside. It becomes a tire swing.
Once that clicked, the rest of the set fell into place fast.
Vines swing. Orangutans swing. Hammocks swing.
Tarzan is practically shorthand for swinging through the trees.
The answer was Things that swing.
Looking back, this is one of those boards that only feels obvious after the right action word appears.
solutionNarrative: I first treated the set like a jungle or rainforest category because Vines, Orangutans, and Hammocks all live comfortably in that picture. That read was plausible, but it stayed too broad and never explained why the board wanted an everyday object like Old tires.

The turn came when I read Old tires as tire swing instead of as junk lying around outside. Once swing became the shared action, the rest of the board tightened immediately: vines swing, orangutans swing, hammocks swing, and Tarzan is the most obvious swinging image of all.

wordHints.Vines: Vines fit because they are one of the most familiar things people swing from, not just part of a jungle setting.
wordHints.Orangutans: Orangutans fit because they are strongly associated with swinging through branches rather than simply living in the jungle.
wordHints.Hammocks: Hammocks belong because their most familiar motion is a gentle swing once they are suspended.
wordHints.Old tires: Old tires is the real turning clue because the natural phrase is tire swing, which makes the action explicit.
wordHints.Tarzan: Tarzan confirms the answer because the character is iconic for swinging on vines rather than merely appearing in a jungle.

spoilerHints.Vines: Think less about location and more about what this clue does once it hangs freely.
spoilerHints.Orangutans: This clue works better as a motion clue than as a habitat clue.
spoilerHints.Hammocks: The clean fit appears once you focus on movement instead of scenery.
spoilerHints.Old tires: This is the clue that turns the board from a setting into one action.
spoilerHints.Tarzan: A famous image tied to this clue should confirm the same physical motion.

lessons.title: Do not stop at the setting if the action is stronger
lessons.body: A board can look like it is describing one place, but the better answer is often the action that ties every clue together.

lessons.title: Watch for the clue that turns a scene into a specific action
lessons.body: Old tires matters because it points to tire swing, which makes the rest of the clues snap into the same motion-based reading.

lessons.title: Re-check every clue once the verb appears
lessons.body: Once swing showed up as the real connector, each clue could be tested quickly against the same action instead of a vague scene.
